Prepare a model for simulation on this process, once

Source: R/parallel.R
simtte_prepare_model.Rd

Builds (or, if this process has already built the exact same model before – mread_cache's/mcode_cache's own in-session cache – reuses) and loadsos a model, returning it wrapped in a class sim_tte_ode recognizes and never rebuilds. sim_tte_ode calls this function internally for every model it is given (a character library name, a tte_model-converted simtte_model, or an object this function already returned) – there is exactly one model-loading path, whether or not a caller prepares anything ahead of time.

Usage

simtte_prepare_model(model, knots = NULL)

Arguments

model

A character library-model name (as sim_tte_ode's own model argument), a simtte_model from tte_model, or an object this function already returned.

knots

Only used, and required, when model = "mspline": its length selects which of the three shipped knot-count variants (?sim_tte_ode "M-spline knot-count variants") gets compiled – the knot values themselves, like coefs/boundary_knots, only ever affect $PARAM values, applied later by sim_tte_ode itself, never which compiled variant is loaded (checked directly: this function's only use of knots is length(knots)). coefs/ boundary_knots are therefore not parameters of this function at all – supplying either raises R's own "unused argument" error, naming it, rather than silently accepting a value that would not affect what gets built.

Value

An object of class "simtte_prepared_model". Pass it directly as sim_tte_ode's own model argument.

Details

The point of calling this yourself: a parallel PSOCK worker is a separate R process with no memory of what the parent process has already built or loaded. Calling sim_tte_ode() directly, unprepared, on each worker is not wrong – every path through it now calls loadso – but it does mean each worker independently pays its own full compile cost the first time (harmless for a fast-compiling built-in model; measured up to ~1.5s for a tte_model()-converted one, "Parallel simulation" section of ?sim_tte_ode). Calling simtte_prepare_model() once per worker at cluster initialization avoids that redundant work and is the pattern verified race-free: a worker receiving an already-compiled model object (via ordinary parallel serialization – parallel::clusterCall()/clusterExport() both work) and only ever calling loadso() on it never races, unlike a worker independently re-triggering mcode_cache()/mread_cache() against a directory another process might be writing to at the same time.

Idempotent: calling this on its own return value (exactly what happens when the same model = argument is broadcast to every worker via clusterCall(), each worker then calling this function on it again) only re-loadso()s (cheap, safe to repeat) and returns the object unchanged – never a second build.

A genuinely separate process (not a parallel cluster worker that received the compiled object by serialization, but e.g. a chunked/array-job task reading a tte_model object back from a manifest file written by an earlier, already-exited process): a simtte_model's compiled shared object lives wherever the building process's own cache put it, which a later process cannot see. Calling this function there rebuilds it from $code/$name automatically, into this process's own simtte_model_cache – deterministic (the same code and name always produce the same compiled model), and never a global mrgsolve option, so correctness never depends on the two processes sharing a filesystem. A built-in library model needs no such rebuild (it is always (re)built from the shipped .cpp source into this process's own cache directly, every time).

See also

sim_tte_ode, which takes the returned object as model (see "Parallel simulation" there for the full cluster-init pattern). tte_model, which builds the simtte_model to pass in for your own model. simtte_model_cache, where the compiled model is stored, and simtte_model_cache_clear, to remove it.

Examples

# \donttest{
prepared <- simtte_prepare_model("exponential")
#> Building exponential_ode ... 
#> done.
sim <- sim_tte_ode(model = prepared, param = list(H0 = 0.1), n = 10,
  end = 20, delta = 2, seed = 1)
head(sim$events)
#>   ID   sim_time sim_status sim_reason
#> 1  1 13.2610805          1      event
#> 2  2  9.8852799          1      event
#> 3  3  5.5712546          1      event
#> 4  4  0.9628203          1      event
#> 5  5 16.0106348          1      event
#> 6  6  1.0715139          1      event
# }
